currentCanonicalDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann CO₂-Bilanzen und Reaktionswärmen verschiedener Brennstoffe auf einer vergleichbaren Bezugsgröße und innerhalb derselben Systemgrenze gegenüberstellen.

findings.detail: Both rows now show fuel pointing to a combustion flame, with two separate arrows branching from that flame to heat waves and CO₂. The former visible heat → CO₂ causal chain is absent. The image correctly treats heat release and CO₂ as concurrent outputs of complete combustion.

The identical heat motifs in both rows make the 'GLEICHE WÄRME' basis visible. The methane row has the smaller CO₂ cloud and the pure-carbon row the larger one. This is the correct qualitative direction for the same released heat from complete combustion: CH₄ and C each yield one CO₂ per mole of fuel, while a mole of CH₄ releases more heat than a mole of C. The clouds do not assert a numerical ratio.

Actual native 1448x1086, 680x510 and 360x270 pixels were inspected. The title, 'METHAN (CH₄)', 'KOHLENSTOFF (C)' and CO₂ labels remain readable at 360 px; the branching arrows, equal heat symbols and cloud-size difference remain distinct. There is no crop, required tiny type or visual crowding. The 4:3 image gives two rows enough height on a phone and is a justified exception to the 16:9 default. Its warm, abstract comic style fits the existing visual landscape.

The active 2752x1536 JPG was also inspected at native width and proportionally reduced to 360x201. Its table writing is mostly too small at phone width. More seriously, it juxtaposes CO₂ per mole with unquantified 'hoch'/'mittel' reaction heat and unsupported categorical suitability marks. Replacing it is justified by specific weaknesses rather than by format normalization.

The drawing is a qualitative direct-combustion comparison, not a full CO₂ balance or lifecycle assessment. It omits the methane combustion water product because it selects the two outputs relevant to this contrast; it must not be presented as a complete reaction equation. The lower black solid resembles coal, but the visible 'KOHLENSTOFF (C)' label identifies the intended pure-carbon model. Prospective alt text and P evidence should explicitly distinguish pure C from compositionally variable coal, name equal released heat and direct CO₂, and address wider system boundaries separately.

sourceScope: Bavaria Chemie 8 provides the curricular setting for comparing fuel CO₂ and reaction energy; the EIA heat-content table supports the qualitative natural-gas versus coal direction but is not treated as data for pure C. The pure-CH₄ versus pure-C comparison was checked from complete-combustion stoichiometry and relative heat release.
